final_text: The British Red Cross is here to help people in crisis in the UK and around the world. We're an emergency response organisation. That is the heart of our mission. For us, the outcomes we want to have are humanitarian outcomes. We want to be able to better plan. We want to ensure that we can drive operational efficiencies, but also meet unmet need where that is greatest. If we can't make decisions in near real time.Time. How do we then act and respond appropriately? Part of the approach we're taking with DataBricks is to build the capabilities we have, so that data can flow through the organisation. For us, the data architecture and a modern data platform like DataBricks allows us to utilise data engineering effectively by identifying the sources of fragmented data that we have, so that we can join that data up in a connected.way to reduce duplication of effort, improve our costs, improve opportunities around efficiency and robustness of that architecture. We use Unity Catalog to be able to centralise structured and unstructured data into one secure place. It allows us then to identify where data is. It identifies what the governance controls and access we need to put around that data so that we can be secure about the way that people access and use.Data with confidence and trust. For example, during a large fundraising appeal, there can be millions of pounds of income, and that translates into millions of records that we need to process and then put in the hands of decision makers to inform our investment plans in near real time. The DataBricks platform allows us to achieve that kind of scale securely and robustly. We've reduced our time down to a few hours to be able to.The data quickly in the hands of some of our fundraisers to understand the performance of the activity, to then understand how we best apply that to attract more people to our marketing. Ultimately, every amount of money we spend or fundraise is then allowing us to achieve our mission, so helping people in crisis in the UK and overseas.
